name: AI trade jitters
backstory: Markets leaned on the very largest AI-linked tech companies, so doubts about AI hit the whole [[index]]. Nvidia's CEO left on Nov 12 and an AI selloff followed. Since then, official papers have warned that AI [[valuation]]s look stretched, and the S&P 500 fell four straight weeks.
today: Nvidia's board approved Huang's return and the stock rose 30% or more. Trump told CNBC 'I made the deal'. Tech rallied, and the Nasdaq was up nearly 7% at midday. A headline calls Nvidia the 'central bank of AI', meaning one firm now steers the market's mood. Analysts split on whether this is a bottom or a short rebound.

name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up [[headline inflation]]. Central banks must decide whether it fades or leaks into wages and services. The euro area hit 4% inflation, the Bank of England hiked to 4%, and the Fed sits at 3.875%.
today: A headline says Fed rate-hike odds jumped as Nvidia saved the day. Earlier, St. Louis Fed's Musalem said four more hikes may be needed. UK inflation hit 3.6% on record diesel prices, and Japan's core inflation hit its highest this year. Waller said the Fed meets Dec 8 and 9. Treasury yields and the dollar both rose today.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict that began in early 2026 cut global oil output by 12 mb/d in March. Prices jumped but not to records, because stored oil filled the gap. Tensions eased in June and then returned.
today: WTI fell 3.64% to 80.92 on more Middle East flows and a Libyan pipeline restart. Tanker attacks continue, so the war is not over. The IEA says the Hormuz shock lifted the world's oil and gas import bill 25% to $1.6 trillion. Fed Governor Cook said damaged infrastructure and low inventories could keep oil prices high for a long time.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout. Markets ask how divided government would change tariffs, spending and the dollar. The dollar has had its biggest rally since 2024.
today: The dollar index rose 0.64% to 104.47. Headlines tie the move to hawkish Fed bets and the AI rally, not the election. Friday's headline said the Fed-fueled rally stalled and lower US yields helped the yen. Gold rebounded 3.99% after its sharpest weekly drop since March. Trump also suggested gas price drops are linked to the election.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the currency market, including a record $50 billion in one day. The BOJ's 1.25% rate is 2.625 percentage points below the Fed's 3.875%, which encourages selling yen to hold dollars. Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank in Q3 as energy costs bit.
today: USD/JPY was 159.32, down 0.04%, so the yen was little changed. The BOJ chief played down soft consumption data and signaled a near-term rate hike. Japan's inflation accelerated, and the country posted a sixth straight monthly trade deficit. A Reuters-style analysis says BOJ ambiguity on the path of hikes could tempt yen bears. In Friday's Asian session, the Nikkei fell 2.9% on chip and metals stocks.
